_comment: Model registry. Add any model here — cloud API, local Ollama, whatever.
The harness will test it and tell you if your tier_ceiling guess is right.
Fields:
provider:      anthropic | openai | deepseek | mistral | google | ollama | openai-compat
input_per_1M:  USD per 1M input tokens (0 for local models)
output_per_1M: USD per 1M output tokens (0 for local models)
tier_ceiling:  highest tier you think this model can handle (T0-T5)
base_url:      (optional) for openai-compat providers, the API base URL
api_key_env:   (optional) env var name for the API key
To add a HuggingFace model running locally via Ollama:
1. ollama pull <model-name>
2. Add an entry below with provider: 'ollama' and costs: 0
3. Run: python orchestrator.py --benchmark T0
4. Check if it passes. Adjust tier_ceiling based on results.
STALENESS: models ship monthly and prices drift. This registry rots
silently unless reviewed against the providers' own pricing pages.
Last reviewed: 2026-07-07 (anthropic line refreshed to current: opus-4-8,
sonnet-5, haiku-4-5, fable-5; openai gpt-5.5 + google gemini 3.x/3.5
verified; other openai/mistral/deepseek entries carried forward unverified).

AXIS NOTE (2026-07-08): tier_ceiling is a DECLARED hypothesis (read: declared_tier_ceiling), kept for backward compatibility. The measured axis is settled-vs-derived work — see the 'measured' block on models with evidence, HYPOTHESES.md H2/H6, and experiments/breadth/run/waterline.json. Do not add 'measured' blocks without sediment-layer evidence.

_comment: Named roles decouple 'who does what' from model names, which churn.
driver: plans, verifies, and repairs — spends judgment tokens only.
The orchestrator uses roles.driver as its planner; override per-run
with --driver or the TIER_BENCH_DRIVER env var. Execution ('hands')
always auto-routes to the cheapest capable model, never the driver.
apprentice: a cheaper model being taught the driver role. Set it as
--driver and score it with diff_report --target <apprentice> to see
how close it is to replicating the frontier driver. See driver/README.md.
Composite candidates: compositions benchmarked as first-class rows,
so 'cheap model + harness replicates the frontier model' is a measured
claim. Strategies: cascade (escalate through members on failure),
best_of_n (resample one member; task validators select), driver_repair
(hands model attempts; on failure the driver gets the failed output +
validator report as evidence and produces the repair). A composite is
priced by EVERY call it makes, failures included.
